description: How far a video has been played, and when it is watched. Drive carries the position; every client works out the rest. In each case `entry` is the video's merged watched entry (absent when it has none) and `duration` the video's length in seconds as the client knows it (absent or 0 when unknown); `op` says what is checked. An entry's `position` counts only when it is a number that is not negative; anything else reads as no position. `watched`: whether the video is watched; `expected` is a boolean. It is watched when the entry's `watched` is true, or when it has a position, `duration` is greater than 10 and `position` >= `duration` - 10 (within the last 10 seconds of its length). So a video of 10 seconds or less, or of unknown length, is watched only by `watched: true`, and an old entry with `watched: true` and no position is watched as before. `resume`: where the video starts when opened; `expected` is in seconds. 0 when it is watched by the rule above or has no position; otherwise its position. `bar`: the progress bar along the bottom of the video's thumbnail; `expected` is the filled fraction from 0 to 1, or null for no bar. 1 when it is watched by the rule above; otherwise null without a position or without a `duration` greater than 0; otherwise `position` / `duration`. A fraction of 0 draws nothing. A playlist has no position and no bar: only `watched` counts for it. What a client writes, always under the item's id in its own file with `at` set to now, keeping any unknown fields the entry had: (1) while a video plays in its own player, `watched: false` and `position` as the player reports it — often on the device (every few seconds), and to Drive with the usual delayed upload only on pause, on leaving the player and when the app goes to the background, never every few seconds; nothing is written for a live broadcast, or before playback starts. (2) when the player reports the end, `watched: true` and `position` as reported; nothing more is written for that video until it plays again, and playing it again writes (1), which is how moving back in a watched video makes it unwatched with the new position. (3) a mark made without playing — setup's starting point, a playlist's last video ending, a mark made by hand — `watched: true`, leaving `position` as it was. (4) an unmark made by hand: `watched: false` and `position` removed. Leaving a video part-way therefore keeps its position and leaves it in the feed. The unwatched counts count every video that is not watched by the rule above, so a part-watched one counts.
